description: The provided image is a multi-layered pie chart illustrating the ethical principles and corresponding obligations in medical ethics, likely serving as a conceptual framework for the MedEthicsQA benchmark. The chart is organized around four core principles—Beneficence (blue), Non-Maleficence (purple), Autonomy (green), and Justice (orange)—each represented as a major segment in the inner circle. Radiating outward from each principle are specific ethical duties or actions, forming wedge-shaped segments in the outer ring that are color-coded to match their parent principle. Beneficence, the largest segment, includes obligations such as “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” “Respect Life, Dignity of Patients,” and “Ethical research.” Non-Maleficence encompasses duties like “Prevent Patient from Harm,” “Maintain Qualified When Providing Medical Care,” and “Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain.” Autonomy includes “Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed,” “Keep Confidential,” and “Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve.” Justice covers “Promote the Health of Community and Public Education,” “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” and “Treat Patients Fairly and Equally.” The chart visually emphasizes the hierarchical structure of medical ethics, mapping abstract principles to concrete professional responsibilities, and likely underpins the question categories used to evaluate LLMs in the MedEthicsQA benchmark.
